content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (fallback cure).**

The agreement locks Tri City into a minimum Monthly Base Fee (§ 8.1(ii)), payable in advance by ACH debit (§ 8.13), and § 10.3(A) requires Customer to source *every* Service in that bundle from M&I for the full eight-year Term (§ 1.X) with no descope right — while the only exit (§ 11.1) costs a year's notice plus a percentage of Estimated Remaining Value computed off that same minimum. That is textbook multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction right, i.e. walk-away territory.

Cure taken at the **fallback** level (preferred deletion would require collateral rewrites to §§ 8.1, 8.13 and the Estimated Remaining Value definition):

1. § 10.3(A) — commitment narrowed from "during the Term" to "during the then-current twelve (12) month period of the Term only", preserving all other words verbatim.
2. New § 10.3(B) — 30 days' notice right to reduce the bundled Services and corresponding commitment, with any shortfall trued up to Services actually ordered and used "and not as a penalty".

The § 11.1 convenience fee is left untouched here, as it belongs to the termination-rights rule and should not be double-flagged.
